properties.label: 30x30x1 mesh QP gap
properties.definition: CBM minus VBM over the 900 points of the 30x30x1 fine mesh used as the BSE transition grid. 30 is divisible by 3, so K is on this mesh and the value coincides with the K-point path gap.

properties.label: Lowest bright singlet excitation (30x30 fine grid)
properties.definition: Lowest TDA singlet root carrying oscillator strength in the 1-5 eV window on the 900-point fine grid; the bare lowest eigenvalue is dark.

properties.label: Exciton binding energy (30x30 fine grid)
properties.definition: 30x30x1 mesh QP gap 2.39727 eV minus the 1.942436 eV lowest bright excitation. Screening and RI come from the coarser 14x14x1 grid, which is the dual-grid approximation this record documents.

properties.label: Strongest absorption peak (30x30 fine grid)
properties.definition: Global maximum of eps2(w) in the 1-5 eV window at 0.10 eV broadening.

properties.label: eps2 at the strongest peak
properties.definition: eps2 includes the 2 pi^2/(N_k V) factor with the primitive-cell volume 1777.44 bohr^3 (|a1 x a2| . c) and the f_file/2 correction, and is checked against the f-sum rule. The raw spectrum_* file is an extensive quantity and is not eps2.

scientific_scope.transition_grid: coarse 14x14x1 (196 k) for screening and RI, fine 30x30x1 (900 k) for the BSE transition space
caveats: Screening and the RI coefficients come from the 14x14x1 grid while the transition space uses 30x30x1. This is the dual-grid approximation LibBSE supports through bse_use_fine_kgrid=1; it is not a fully self-consistent 30x30 screening.
The G0W0 steps used the pyatb velocity source that reads the velocity_matrix ABACUS wrote, not the native H(R)/S(R)/r(R) differentiation.

The 14x14x1 mesh does not contain K, so its mesh gap 2.52630 eV is a sampled value below the K-point gap. The 30x30x1 mesh does contain K, so the fine-grid gap 2.39727 eV coincides with the K-point path gap. The two binding energies are quoted against their own grid gap and must not be compared to each other directly.

eps2 is normalised by the primitive-cell volume 1777.44 bohr^3, taken from |a1 x a2| . c with a1 = 3.184 A and c = 30 A. The hexagonal form (sqrt(3)/2) a^2 c gives the same number; multiplying it by 3 is a common slip and would understate eps2 by a factor of three.
The eps2 normalisation was checked against the f-sum rule: integrating omega*eps2 to 30 eV reproduces the analytic 2*pi^2*sum(f_phys)/(N_k*V) to 0.1%.

The exciton density slices were reconstructed with a wrapper around alter_excitons_gw_bse_20261105/scripts/exciton_density_from_amplitudes.py, patched in three documented ways: the l<=3 harmonics (this basis has an f shell), per-species orbital widths (Mo 44, S 22), and the LibBSE band-window offset 9. Without the offset the electron density peaks at S rather than at Mo.

The 30x30 path band tables carry only the 8 near-gap states requested by i_state_low/high; the 88-band path tables and the frontier figures come from the separate 121-point path run on the same SCF density.
